newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB sees digital decoder at 200/300 stg.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB sees digital decoder at 200/300 stg.

text.p: British satellite broadcaster BSkyB Plc is hoping that digital set-top boxes can be priced at between 200 and 300 stg when it launches its new digital service late next year.

"The cost of the box should be between 200-300 pounds to encourage people to buy it," BSkyB chairman Gerry Robinson told the company's Annual General Meeting. "At that price it has to be quite heavily subsidised," he added.

BSkyB is planning to launch some 200 digital channels into Britain next autumn. It is reported to be talking to possible partners such as British Telecommunications about subsidising the set-top decoders.
As well as greatly increasing channel capacity, digital television will allow for interactivity through the decoder and the launch of services such as home shopping and home banking.
BSkyB has expanded into Germany, with a deal to take a stake of up to 49 percent in Leo Kirch's DF1 digital satellite service which was launched in July.

"Germany is the next important market. We believe there is tremendous upside there," Robinson said. Germany is Europe's biggest television market with some 32 million households against 22 million in the UK.
